newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party misreported spending - agency.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party misreported spending - agency.

text.p: Mexico's electoral watchdog fined the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) for irregularities in reporting its campaign spending last year, officials said on Saturday.

The PRI was fined 5.46 million pesos (about $690,000) for not detailing how it spent some 19 million pesos ($2.4 million) in public money in 1996, officials at the Federal Electoral Commission (IFE) said.
The action was taken on Friday after five hours of heated debate between the PRI and the electoral group, which was given autonomy from the government in the past year by President Ernesto Zedillo.

Members of the PRI, which has governed the country for 68 years, accused the IFE of targeting the ruling party and favouring the opposition. They pledged to appeal the decision to an electoral tribunal.
Two small opposition parties, the Workers' Party (PT) and the Popular Socialist Party (PPS), were fined smaller amounts for misreporting campaign spending, the electoral commission said.
